Alex / Marcus — jumping in with the short technical explainer and the estimator CSV attached. TL;DR answers first, then a brief rationale.

Answers:
- Billing unit: Redwood bills primarily on model tokens (input + output tokens consumed by the model). Requests are recorded for quota/rate but are not a billing unit.
- Caching: Perfect cache hits (where the full response is served from a Redis-like cache without invoking the model runtime) do not incur model token costs. Partial cache reuse can reduce billed tokens only if the cached prefix eliminates the model work for that portion — the runtime still bills tokens for any model invocation that occurs.
- Character -> token rule of thumb: for English text, assume ~4 characters per token (so 250 characters ≈ 62 tokens). This varies by language and punctuation; we attached a CSV with tokenizer samples across typical prompts.

Concrete examples (for budgeting):
- Example A: user prompt 250 chars (~62 tokens) + system metadata 80 chars (~20 tokens) + expected response 120 tokens = billed tokens when model invoked: 62+20+120 = 202 tokens.
- Example B: with 30% perfect cache reuse on the prompt+system combo, 30% of requests are served without model invocation → billed tokens = 0 for those hits. Effective billed-token reduction ≈ 30% (assuming identical responses).
- Note on partial caching: if only the prompt prefix is cached, the model still runs for the uncached remainder; billed tokens reflect what the model processes in that invocation.

Practical guidance for the quote we’ll produce:
- We will show three scenarios: no cache (baseline), 30% perfect-hit cache, and 60% perfect-hit cache. Each scenario will compute monthly billed tokens and convert to effective $/1M billed tokens at your target price points so you can compare.
- For peak-hour provisioning we can show both reserved throughput (to guarantee latency) and burstable pricing if you prefer a lower reserved commitment.

Attachments included: billing-metric-one-pager.pdf (short explainer), sample-tokenizer-estimates.csv (rows: sample_text, chars, tokens_estimate).

If you want, I can also add a column to the CSV that computes estimated monthly billed tokens given your 15M prompts/day assumption and a chosen response length distribution.
